headline.text: The FDA label says trazodone may increase alcohol's CNS-depressant effects.

reported.text: A small crossover study found further impairment of manual dexterity with the combination, while other measured effects changed little.

claims.text: The FDA label says trazodone may increase alcohol's CNS-depressant effects.
claims.quote: Trazodone hydrochloride tablets may enhance effects of alcohol
claims.judgeRationale: Under its CNS-depressants heading the label says trazodone may enhance the effects of alcohol.

claims.text: A six-volunteer crossover study reported further impairment of manual dexterity when ethanol was combined with trazodone, with little additional effect on other measures.
claims.quote: In combination with either trazodone or amitriptyline, ethanol caused little additional effect except in the case of manual dexterity, which was further impaired.
claims.judgeRationale: The six-volunteer double-blind crossover abstract reports little additional effect from ethanol except further impaired manual dexterity.
